scope: Development study of a temporal-smoothness continuation scheduler: train on smoother motion schedules (transition width w > 1/2) and finish on the original problem (w = 1/2) with the same total budget as v2. Paired with the v2 analytic runs on the same seeds.

training.start: fresh original initialization; no direct-velocity checkpoints
training.stop_rule: none; the full budget runs; the first original-problem closure meeting both training limits is recorded with its parameters
training.engine: packed activation with analytic transpose, compiled, CUDA Graph replay; one graph per stage
training.gradient_reference: dense eager C36 parameter AD at the stage width (chunk 128); preserved full native AD for the original problem at the initial parameters
training.stage_rules: Adam state carries across stages; the learning rate follows the global update index; L-BFGS restarts at every stage; the training gate and loss thresholds count only events of the original problem

physical.state_observer: native coordinate AD of the trained curl-potential network

saved_state: scheduled checkpoints, the first training-gate closure and all loss/gradient events
gradient_checks: every 50 L-BFGS calls and at scheduled Adam updates
changes_from_v1.unchanged: data, calibration, eta, model, normalization, Adam schedule, L-BFGS settings, seeds, training limits and every physical gate

physical_observation.observer: unchanged box376.potential_physical at the original schedule, independent reader box376.audit_potential_run

decision_rule.a: Loss stays above 1e-4: the problem is budget-, capacity- or sampling-limited at this scale; no formal v3 on budget alone.
decision_rule.b: Loss passes 1e-4 but physical errors stop falling: training objective or sampling does not control the physical gates; change the problem definition explicitly in a new protocol.
decision_rule.c: Physical gates pass: freeze a formal v3 with new seeds generated and stored on the cluster runtime and both engines (compiled packed analytic and equally compiled parameter AD) for time to accepted accuracy.

execution.allocation: one new ACC node, four H100 lanes, one (seed, schedule) per lane; training only, followed by a separate all-planes observation batch

smoothness_parameter.name: motion schedule transition width w
smoothness_parameter.definition: s_w(t) = switch(t/w - (1/(2w) - 1/2)); the box moves for t in (1/2 - w/2, 1/2 + w/2); k-th time derivatives scale as w^-k
smoothness_parameter.implementation: box376.schedule_family (new file; pinned source, geometry and model modules unchanged and swapped in only while a width-w problem is prepared)
smoothness_parameter.verification: box376.test_schedule_family: bitwise identity at w = 1/2; derivative scaling and window; zero value targets; at w = 3/4 the analytic objective and parameter AD agree with an independent native coordinate-AD oracle within the original budget

baseline.runs: v2 development analytic runs, seeds 361901 and 361902 (same engine, data, initial bytes, Adam schedule, L-BFGS settings and total budget, with w = 1/2 throughout)

paired_statistics: per seed and schedule: training seconds and evaluations from the start to the first original-problem loss at or below 1e-3, 3e-4, 1e-4, 3e-5, 1e-5, compared with the v2 analytic run of the same seed
final loss and gradient infinity norm at equal total budget
physical metrics of matched checkpoints on all planes

decision_rule.helps: both schedules or one schedule reach every threshold sooner and the final physical errors (stratified pressure in particular) are lower than the baseline on both seeds
decision_rule.no_effect: differences within the seed-to-seed spread of the baseline
decision_rule.hurts: thresholds reached later or final errors higher on both seeds

analysis.status: development: v1 seeds; not a formal time-to-accuracy result
